title: Late Charge Amount Schedule for the Operating Lines of Credit
content:
The late charge on an Operating Lines of Credit interest bill is a percentage of the bill's charge base, held between the product's minimum and maximum late charge.

## Clause

The charge is figured on the bill it is assessed on — the line's interest bill with the latest due date. The charge base is the bill's billed amount less the interest payments applied to it, with the bill's AutoDraft debit added back when it came back unpaid. The late charge is the charge base multiplied by the product's late charge percentage, read as a percentage, rounded to cents, and then kept no lower than the product's minimum late charge and no higher than its maximum late charge.

The billed amount, the due date and the payments applied to the bill are read from the line's transaction history; a payment is applied to a bill when it points to that bill.

## Schedule of worked figures (hypothetical Revolving Operating Line bills; 5%, minimum USD 35, maximum USD 750)

| Billed amount | Interest payments applied | AutoDraft debit returned unpaid | Charge base | Charge base times 5%, rounded | Late charge |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| USD 4,321.00 | USD 1,000.00 | None | USD 3,321.00 | USD 166.05 | USD 166.05 |
| USD 4,321.00 | USD 1,000.00, an AutoDraft debit later returned | USD 1,000.00 | USD 4,321.00 | USD 216.05 | USD 216.05 |
| USD 400.00 | None | None | USD 400.00 | USD 20.00 | USD 35.00 — raised to the minimum |
| USD 18,000.00 | None | None | USD 18,000.00 | USD 900.00 | USD 750.00 — held to the maximum |

## Point of judgement

The minimum and the maximum act on the figure after it is rounded to cents: a rounded figure below the minimum becomes the minimum, and one above the maximum becomes the maximum.
